RD01.name: Optional package and coordinated release
RD01.contract: @getforma/router owns router policy; core remains a peer. Additive compiler/build/server contracts travel in the matching release set.

RD02.name: Explicit bounded route grammar
RD02.contract: Rank complete branches, static before parameter before terminal splat; support nested/index/pathless layouts. Reject unsupported syntax; preserve search/hash and segment decoding.

RD03.name: Platform semantics first
RD03.contract: Intercept only admitted links and opted-in forms. Keep real href/action/method, browser validation and submitter behavior.

RD04.name: Owned navigation transaction
RD04.contract: Generation identity plus abort, detached preparation, serialized synchronous commit, late-resource disposal and distinct terminal outcomes.

RD05.name: Central history and blockers
RD05.contract: Commit PUSH/REPLACE after admission; POP never pushes. Entry keys/indexes, committed versus pending URL, explicit blocked/foreign-entry recovery.

RD06.name: Persistent layout owners
RD06.contract: Retain only a compatible common owner chain and live nodes; replace changed identity/props boundaries; dispose departing and obsolete owners.

RD07.name: Typed native transition and scoped adoption
RD07.contract: Same typed Rust page produces a versioned navigation response; validate incoming claims in a new scope without resetting original-document authority.

RD08.name: Policy, build and integrity admission
RD08.contract: Require compatible app/build/group/policy; no client-supplied nonce or arbitrary script replay; one bounded safe document recovery.
RD08.owner: forma-server policy, build assets, router admission

RD09.name: Initial group registration bootstrap
RD09.contract: Aggregate registration-only products into an integrity-checked complete executable artifact; defer route-code lazy loading and lazy discovery.

RD10.name: Enhanced Rust forms
RD10.contract: Progressive GET/POST with typed success/validation/error/303 outcomes, no JavaScript server runtime and no client authorization.
RD10.owner: Router forms, forma-server action response, application handlers

RD11.name: Mutation/read generations
RD11.contract: One managed mutation, explicit busy state; invalidate stale reads, revalidate current branch after settlement, suppress obsolete redirects, never replay an uncertain POST.
RD11.owner: Router data coordinator, application mutation policy

RD12.name: Observable experience and completion
RD12.contract: Separate commit from island readiness; owned title/focus/scroll/announcements, reduced motion and browser-native escapes.

RD13.name: Bounded speculation, no private page cache
RD13.contract: Private/native prefetch off by default; explicitly safe intent reads, at most two in flight, no retained completed private HTML or inferred shared TTL.

RD14.name: Status-aware error and fallback
RD14.contract: Not-found/validation/cancel/redirect/failure differ. Keep valid rendered errors; fallback only through the documented method-safe matrix.

RD15.name: Evidence and source ownership
RD15.contract: Keep source, artifact, REA, browser and original-prototype evidence distinct; retain pins, raw failures, licenses and scope limits.

RD16.name: Native proof before expansion
RD16.contract: Original examples are scaffolds, not framework qualification. Prove native policy/adoption/forms first, then qualify the full opt-in feature.

questions.question: Where is the actual implementation?
questions.conclusion: Keep router/library and docs ownership pinned; no host or byte-attestation inference.

questions.question: Where is the docs app hosted?
questions.conclusion: Retain Firebase configuration only as hosting evidence; it does not select Forma hosting.

questions.question: Is the docs site actually client routed?
questions.conclusion: Use document identity and requests to prove routing; the single Chromium sample is not cross-browser credit.

questions.question: Can REA recover the complete router or route table from these minified bundles?
questions.conclusion: Keep truncated REA graphs and selected-source limits; source and executable tests close different gaps.

questions.question: What must the URL parser preserve?
questions.conclusion: Preserve segment encoding/query repetition/hash; do not import Angular matrix/named-outlet grammar or host-specific slash predecode.

questions.question: What does “first match wins” actually mean?
questions.conclusion: Keep full-branch recognition; choose ranked Forma precedence rather than Angular configuration-order semantics.

questions.question: Are routes limited to flat paths?
questions.conclusion: Adopt nested/index/pathless layouts; defer named outlets and nonterminal multi-pattern wildcards.

questions.question: How are redirect loops bounded?
questions.conclusion: Redirect is a bounded control outcome; choose a Forma limit rather than copy Angular's development/production constant behavior.

questions.question: What keeps a slow earlier navigation from overwriting a later one?
questions.conclusion: Generation checks supplement abort and cover synchronous callbacks as well as promises.

questions.question: Are same-URL requests always ignored?
questions.conclusion: Separate same-URL skip, explicit data revalidation and owner recreation.

questions.question: Does a link click always call pushState?
questions.conclusion: Use History API first; Navigation API integration is deferred because one docs Chromium path cannot establish supported-engine behavior.

questions.question: Why is cancelling Back harder than cancelling a link?
questions.conclusion: Restore/replay known POP deltas; never repair cancellation with an extra push.

questions.question: Which anchor actions should stay native?
questions.conclusion: Keep real hrefs and complete native-action escapes; do not extract a site-specific click helper without negative cases.

questions.question: When do guards, data, code, and DOM run?
questions.conclusion: Order matching/leaving checks/preparation/commit/settling explicitly; loading code and DOM activation have different ownership.

questions.question: Do all Angular loaders run in parallel?
questions.conclusion: Document data dependencies instead of claiming every loader runs in parallel; native destination preparation is a typed server response.

questions.question: How does this site get the next document body?
questions.conclusion: Do not copy the docs Promise-per-path HTML cache or its retained 404 rejection into private native routing.

questions.question: Does cancellation stop the content network request?
questions.conclusion: Cancellation of one consumer is not proof shared network work stopped; revoke commit authority independently.

questions.question: What is reused during navigation?
questions.conclusion: Reuse stable route/layout identity, not component name or URL alone; changed props/identity replace the boundary.

questions.question: What DOM transformation occurs?
questions.conclusion: Generated HTML is a controlled owned region inside an adapter; never equate it with native claim authority.

questions.question: Is preloading the same as caching?
questions.conclusion: Separate registration bootstrap, speculative data, module preload and HTTP cache.

questions.question: Does this router supply form actions and mutation invalidation?
questions.conclusion: Enhanced Rust actions are an explicit new contract, not an assumed consequence of guards or resolvers.

questions.question: When can scroll restoration happen?
questions.conclusion: Restore scroll after usable layout and only for the current owner.

questions.question: Does updating the title guarantee accessible focus?
questions.conclusion: Title alone does not prove accessible focus/announcements; test these separately.

questions.question: Does client routing eliminate SSR, deep-link, or base-path work?
questions.conclusion: Deep URL, base path and server normalization remain server/build responsibilities.

questions.question: What is the error contract?
questions.conclusion: Separate cancel/redirect/skip/error; preserve server auth and status rather than map every failure to 404.

questions.question: Where is the framework implemented?
questions.conclusion: Keep framework source distinct from docs and theme pins.

questions.question: Where is the docs site implemented?
questions.conclusion: Retain the separate docs snapshot without claiming it is an attested deployed commit.

questions.question: Where is the theme and what hosts docs?
questions.conclusion: Keep Starlight and Cloudflare evidence as provenance, not a Forma deployment dependency.

questions.question: Is the docs site a demonstration of ClientRouter?
questions.conclusion: The observed docs reload is not a ClientRouter runtime test; prove Forma native behavior independently.

questions.question: Could persistent sidebar state mislead us?
questions.conclusion: Stored/restored values do not prove live DOM identity; assert actual objects.

questions.question: Does an `astro:page-load` listener prove ClientRouter is enabled?
questions.conclusion: A router event listener in an asset is not evidence that routing is enabled.

questions.question: Is there a client route tree and outlet matcher?
questions.conclusion: Native server resolves typed destinations, while browser routes need a branch matcher; explicit adapters prevent conflation.

questions.question: How do route conflicts resolve?
questions.conclusion: Use explicit Forma ranked rules and complete-branch tests; do not copy Astro file-route tie-breaks.

questions.question: How does a page opt in?
questions.conclusion: Use an explicit compiler/server capability and group contract, stronger than a marker-only admission test.

questions.question: What click events are intercepted?
questions.conclusion: Adopt composed-path eligibility and native escapes with a negative case for each escape.

questions.question: What gets fetched?
questions.conclusion: Use a typed navigation representation for native pages; full HTML belongs only to its admitted generated-HTML adapter.

questions.question: Can an HTML 404 be rendered?
questions.conclusion: Valid typed 404 content is a status-preserving result, not an automatic network failure.

questions.question: Who wins if slow A finishes after fast B?
questions.conclusion: Newest owner wins; await/serialize the previous commit and revoke stale preparation.

questions.question: Is fetch cancellation alone enough?
questions.conclusion: Abort alone is insufficient at custom async or reentrant boundaries.

questions.question: Can hooks cancel or replace the process?
questions.conclusion: Define explicit blocked/cancelled/native-fallback outcomes; do not reuse Astro event cancellation semantics.

questions.question: What are lifecycle events ordered around?
questions.conclusion: Expose commit and island readiness separately; no page-load claim that all deferred islands finished.

questions.question: What does `await navigate()` mean?
questions.conclusion: Specify navigate outcome plus readiness; animation completion is a separate concern.

questions.question: Are same-URL and fragment navigations identical?
questions.conclusion: Hash, query, self-link and form navigation each have an explicit branch.

questions.question: What happens after redirect?
questions.conclusion: Commit final admitted URL; action redirects preserve method-safe semantics rather than blind fetch-follow.

questions.question: Why remove `noscript` from parsed HTML?
questions.conclusion: Detached parsing needs a typed trust boundary; no-JS markup is not blindly transplanted into the live document.

questions.question: How is CSS ready before the body changes?
questions.conclusion: Wait for admitted CSS with bounded failure handling; load-error settlement is not proof of correct styling.

questions.question: How is the head reconciled?
questions.conclusion: Manage title/metadata/styles explicitly; HTTP policy cannot be replaced by a head swap.

questions.question: Does persistence mean copy old HTML?
questions.conclusion: Persistence retains live nodes, not serialized copies.

questions.question: What about canvas, media, shadow roots?
questions.conclusion: Keep stable layout nodes in place; arbitrary keyed media/canvas/shadow-root transplants are not first-release persistence.

questions.question: Do persisted island props update?
questions.conclusion: Do not silently mutate snapshot props; replace incompatible native layout owners after server revalidation.

questions.question: When does an island unmount?
questions.conclusion: Temporary movement and permanent disposal differ; scoped owners must cancel deferred activation.

questions.question: How are scripts activated and deduplicated?
questions.conclusion: Do not replay/deduplicate fetched scripts. Use compiler-owned registration products and the verified initial bootstrap.

questions.question: How are back/forward direction and scroll known?
questions.conclusion: Keep entry identity, committed URL and scroll snapshots separate from the already-moved browser cursor.

questions.question: What focus/accessibility policy exists?
questions.conclusion: Preserve retained-control focus, announce transitions and test actual keyboard/assistive behavior.

questions.question: Does animation support determine routing support?
questions.conclusion: Routing does not depend on animation API support; reduced-motion behavior is explicit.

questions.question: How do GET/POST forms differ?
questions.conclusion: Preserve native GET/POST/submitter semantics, with a stronger explicit no-replay uncertain-outcome contract.

questions.question: What is prefetch caching?
questions.conclusion: Do not copy an unbounded attempted-URL set or infer a result-cache TTL; share bounded live requests only.

questions.question: Is prefetch safe for every GET?
questions.conclusion: Only explicitly safe server reads may be prefetched; same origin does not make a mutation-on-GET safe.

questions.question: Is there a release mismatch fence?
questions.conclusion: Add explicit build/protocol compatibility; the absence found in two Astro files is not a universal upstream failure claim.

questions.question: Does no JavaScript still work?
questions.conclusion: Keep complete server routes and native forms usable without enhancement.

questions.question: Does REA prove execution or exhaustive route coverage?
questions.conclusion: REA parsed selected artifacts, not execution or exhaustive routing coverage.

questions.question: What did the docs REA alias bound mean?
questions.conclusion: Retain the 512-state alias bound and unknowns; missing graph edges are not negative proof.

questions.question: Was published JS tied cryptographically to the source commit?
questions.conclusion: Registry/package integrity and source tag alignment do not prove reproducible live bytes; preserve separate receipts.

questions.question: Were upstream tests run?
questions.conclusion: Do not report inspected upstream tests as executed; qualify the actual Forma products.

questions.question: What should we build first for Forma?
questions.conclusion: Ticket supersedes a generic HTML prototype: first prove typed native policy/adoption plus enhanced forms.

questions.question: Where is the router implemented?
questions.conclusion: Identify library ownership separately from documentation application code.

questions.question: Where is the docs website application implemented?
questions.conclusion: Keep website snapshot and framework source independently pinned.

questions.question: Which release is being explained?
questions.conclusion: Tie claims to 8.5.0 and exact commits; no default-main substitution.

questions.question: Can we prove the website's deployed Git commit or whole hosting topology?
questions.conclusion: Fly config/headers do not prove the deployed commit or private infrastructure topology.

questions.question: Is this one routing mode?
questions.conclusion: Use explicit renderer/data responsibilities; do not clone React's mode names or rendering runtime.

questions.question: Does navigation replace the HTML document body?
questions.conclusion: Nested owner trees inform persistence; native destination HTML/state has a distinct adoption adapter.

questions.question: Why does `/teams/new` beat `/teams/:id`?
questions.conclusion: Adopt specificity ranking as a contract, without copying implementation scores blindly.

questions.question: How do nesting, index and pathless routes work?
questions.conclusion: Retain ancestor layout metadata; index leaves and pathless owners have explicit rules.

questions.question: What about optional segments, splats and encoded separators?
questions.conclusion: Preserve encoded segment boundaries; defer optional-segment expansion and reject unsupported grammar.

questions.question: Is the new route-pattern engine the deployed default?
questions.conclusion: Do not copy an experimental matcher as the observed default or make Forma depend on it.

questions.question: Which clicks should remain browser actions?
questions.conclusion: Preserve native click behavior and define delegated HTML-link eligibility fully.

questions.question: Are generated Markdown links handled the same way as JSX Links?
questions.conclusion: Do not copy docs host-only interception; enforce full origin, download and defaultPrevented rules.

questions.question: Why do entries need keys and indexes?
questions.conclusion: Separate entry key, traversal index and unrelated user history state.

questions.question: When is the URL committed?
questions.conclusion: Commit PUSH/REPLACE after preparation; POP already moved and never pushes.

questions.question: How can Back be blocked if popstate cannot be canceled?
questions.conclusion: Use known inverse/replay deltas for blockers; foreign entries have explicit recovery.

questions.question: Does observing the browser Navigation API mean the router uses it?
questions.conclusion: Observed Navigation API events do not prove interception by that API.

questions.question: What states must the UI distinguish?
questions.conclusion: Separate committed/pending route, submitting and revalidating state; omit keyed fetcher state in v1.

questions.question: Is AbortController alone enough to avoid stale UI?
questions.conclusion: Generation identity protects commits from promises that ignore abort.

questions.question: Are loaders always sequential or always rerun?
questions.conclusion: After mutations revalidate the active branch; do not assume universal parallel loading or unconditional parent reuse.

questions.question: What is an action versus a loader?
questions.conclusion: Separate safe GET navigation from POST actions and method-aware redirects.

questions.question: What is a fetcher?
questions.conclusion: Independent keyed/background fetchers are later scope; one managed mutation is the explicit v1 concurrency boundary.

questions.question: Does request cancellation undo server writes?
questions.conclusion: Client cancellation cannot roll back server writes; require application idempotency/ordering for stronger semantics.

questions.question: Are error boundaries just 404 pages?
questions.conclusion: Route-local errors may preserve compatible ancestor layouts; 404 is only one error class.

questions.question: How are redirects classified?
questions.conclusion: Represent redirect metadata explicitly; enhanced mutation replay through 307/308 is not supported in v1.

questions.question: What does Framework mode request over the wire?
questions.conclusion: Do not adopt .data/Turbo Stream as Forma's wire format; use its own versioned typed native response.

questions.question: Does every client loader go through that protocol?
questions.conclusion: Browser loaders and application Rust endpoints remain explicit; native rendering alone uses the native navigation contract.

questions.question: Are route discovery, lazy modules and prefetch synonymous?
questions.conclusion: Treat discovery, code loading, data fetching and speculation as separate lifetimes.

questions.question: Is lazy manifest discovery enabled on the docs site?
questions.conclusion: Use initial group metadata/registration; count its complete initial bytes rather than call it lazy discovery.

questions.question: How does generic lazy discovery handle stale releases?
questions.conclusion: Use explicit version validation and bounded recovery; no blanket reload loop or inherited discovery guarantee.

questions.question: Is loader reuse a universal data cache?
questions.conclusion: Loader reuse is not a universal private data cache; retain clear keys/lifetimes and no-store boundaries.

questions.question: What survives route changes?
questions.conclusion: Common route owners may persist, but Forma must prove actual DOM identity and cleanup under its own runtime.

questions.question: What makes deep links work?
questions.conclusion: Every admitted deep link must have a meaningful server response.

questions.question: How is scroll restored?
questions.conclusion: Entry-key scroll and page lifecycle are explicit, including hashes and no-reset behavior.

questions.question: Does the router automatically solve focus and announcements?
questions.conclusion: Focus/live announcements remain specified and tested rather than assumed from routing.

questions.question: Are React transitions and browser View Transitions the same thing?
questions.conclusion: View-transition animation is optional polish after correctness; React scheduling is not a Forma dependency.

questions.question: Can SSR data be ignored and everything fetched again?
questions.conclusion: Initial typed SSR state is authoritative for adoption; do not refetch/remount away its guarantees.

questions.question: How much did REA parse?
questions.conclusion: Retain 6 parsed files, two successful runs and timed-out entry evidence as scoped static analysis.

questions.question: Did REA recover the complete route tree and state machine?
questions.conclusion: Use inert manifest/source to explain actual route structure; generic favicon candidates are not routes.

questions.question: What was actually tested?
questions.conclusion: Historical Chromium/example tests are not upstream, performance or cross-browser qualification.

questions.question: What is the smallest useful reconstruction?
questions.conclusion: Use the coordinator scaffold, but first release must also satisfy native integration and enhanced-form requirements.

tests.assertion: Verify all 105 source-question IDs, immutable pins, input hashes, source-license paths, REA failures and link targets; distinguish source inspection from execution.
Install the packed router outside the monorepo with one compatible core; declarations/exports resolve and a duplicate or incompatible core is refused.
Old/equal/new writer-reader fixtures keep existing compatibility rules; old consumers cannot accidentally accept a new navigation capability.
Non-opt-in and no-JavaScript routes contain zero router bootstrap bytes; coordinated artifact inventory includes router without rewriting historical release evidence.
Round-trip encoded slash, malformed percent, repeated query keys, plus decoding, fragments and prototype-like parameter names without altering grammar or object prototypes.
Static/parameter/splat precedence, full child consumption, index and pathless layouts select the declared complete branch; duplicate/ambiguous configuration has a documented result.
Relative, root-relative and fragment links under a non-root base resolve from the committed view even while a POP destination is pending.
Unsupported optional/matrix/named-outlet or regex grammar is rejected explicitly; bounded deep/large routes do not produce unbounded expansion.
Same URL, explicit revalidation, query-only and fragment-only changes follow distinct policies; fragment navigation cancels obsolete pending page work.
PUSH/REPLACE commit once after preparation; Back/Forward never PUSH; duplicate URL entries retain separate keys and unrelated history state survives.
Block/allow link/API/POP with unsaved state; known traversal deltas restore and replay correctly; foreign entries recover without invented indexes or loops.
pagehide/pageshow, BFCache restore, teardown and reinstall restore history.scrollRestoration and do not duplicate global handlers.
Relative/internal/external/out-of-base redirects preserve final URL, terminate within the declared budget and never commit an intermediate stale route.
Modified/non-primary/defaultPrevented/download/target/external/unsafe/opt-out clicks stay native; composed-path anchors and real hrefs behave correctly.
Held A then successful B, A ignoring abort and stale A errors cannot mutate B DOM, URL, title, focus, scroll or pending state.
A late detached candidate, stylesheet or deferred activation is disposed exactly once after cancellation and cannot acquire committed ownership.
Callbacks and disposal that request another navigation obey the documented re-entry queue/critical-section rule; no interleaved or resurrected commit.
Committed, cancelled, blocked, redirected, failed and fallback outcomes settle once; DOM commit, initial island readiness and deferred readiness are not conflated.
Sibling child navigation preserves the common layout's actual nodes, input state and owner; departed route effects cease.
At least 100 A/B route cycles, cancellation cycles and failures return tracked listeners, effects, observers, timers, workers and pending activations to baseline.
Changed server layout identity, incompatible props or session boundary replaces the affected owner; stale layout data is not retained merely because markup looks equal.
Two real typed Rust routes with distinct islands navigate A to B to A by link and API, retaining Document/layout identity, fresh props and interactive adopted destination nodes.
Original document state/host claims stay frozen; new navigation context cannot authorize foreign/reused/departed hosts or reset an earlier refusal.
Malformed/oversized state, wrong protocol/route/host identity, duplicate host claims and missing registrations fail before destination activation.
User input before activation is preserved; deferred islands that lose their route cannot activate later; initial adoption does not repair or remount served roots.
Direct URL, refresh and JavaScript-disabled links/forms return meaningful full server HTML with correct status and fresh typed props.
Browser-component and generated-HTML routes use their own admitted contract; generated HTML cannot smuggle native state claims, scripts or a second bootstrap.
Fresh nonces under the same normalized policy allow ordinary native transitions; changed CSP/TT/COOP/permissions policy takes one explicit document boundary.
Wrong app/build/group, missing/changed asset or protocol mismatch cannot execute mixed artifacts; supported same-group transitions never count a reload as success.
The group registration artifact and all executable dependencies are integrity checked; concatenated activation entrypoints and unverified dynamic import graphs are refused.
Inert typed state and framework-authored markup do not replay executable script/event handlers; Trusted Types and strict CSP remain enforced.
no-store persists at real HTTP boundary; logout/account change cannot expose completed cached HTML/state or keep incompatible persistent private owners.
Payload/state/route/redirect/prefetch and preparation time limits fail predictably without unbounded allocations or endless pending UI.
Same application handler handles enhanced and native GET/POST; successful mutation revalidates fresh typed server props and no-JS remains usable.
Browser constraint validation, submitter name/value and action/method/enctype overrides, multipart files and controls named submit/method/action are preserved.
Validation retains safe entered values, renders accessible field/form errors, focuses the summary/first invalid control and neither pushes history nor repeats the action.
Double-click and competing managed submissions produce one active request and explicit busy outcome; nothing is silently queued or retried.
GET/prefetch begun before a POST or its settlement cannot remain authoritative after it; mutation generations trigger a fresh current-branch read.
Navigation during POST can complete; the late action cannot redirect back or overwrite a newer route, and known settlement revalidates the current branch.
Server receives POST but response is lost/aborted/invalid: exactly one client send attempt, visible unknown outcome, no automatic retry or native POST fallback.
Missing/invalid CSRF/session/authorization is rejected by real handlers; client guards never authorize writes or reveal protected data.
Supported action 303 is represented explicitly and followed by GET; enhanced 307/308 method replay is refused, and unsupported forms escape before transmission.
Preserve conflict/auth/server statuses and validate typed action outcomes; malformed or policy/build-incompatible action responses cannot become successful UI commits.
Admitted 404 and route errors render the declared boundary/status; offline, wrong media type and parsing errors follow explicit recovery instead of being relabeled not-found.
Each documented fallback has an assertion of one method-safe document GET and state-loss behavior; recovery does not retry indefinitely or satisfy normal-transition tests.
Title, pending/completion announcement and focus policies are independently asserted; focus/selection in retained controls survives when appropriate.
Entry-key scroll restoration, new-route top, encoded/empty hash and interrupted scroll callbacks behave on Back and Forward without scrolling a newer page.
Reduced motion and absence of View Transitions still route correctly; CSS preparation has bounded success/error handling and stale callbacks cannot commit.
Keyboard, screen-reader announcements/errors and mobile interaction are reviewed on the actual native/form fixture; automation is not claimed as full assistive-technology qualification.
Run the native, forms, history and lifecycle fixture in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including mobile viewport/input and a separately documented gesture check.
Private/native prefetch defaults off; opted-in safe reads cap concurrency at two, honor data-saving/offline state and retain no completed private HTML.
Shared in-flight work outlives one cancelled owner only when another needs it; failed attempts are retryable and mutation/session/build changes revoke stale reuse.
Freeze incremental router and complete group-bootstrap gzip budgets before measurement; retain all results and do not raise existing gates implicitly.
Measure cold entry and warm navigation on fixed routes/mobile profile against document-navigation baseline; report percentiles, sample count and failures without cross-framework superiority claims.
Combine the 100-cycle owned-resource count with browser memory observations; distinguish deterministic cleanup assertions from noisy heap measurements.
Execute the documented TSX plus Rust starter commands against packed candidate artifacts outside the repository; no private deep imports.
Pilot only the admitted flow; disable enhancement and atomically restore matching browser/build/server artifacts; verify ordinary document navigation after rollback.
